neighbours.label: the word ' scalar' (and the connective right after it) in scalar multiplication of vectors or matrices
fire: In this course, students learn how to find the product of a scalar and a vector.
When you multiply a matrix by a scalar, every entry gets multiplied by it.
A vector multiplied by a positive scalar keeps its direction but changes length.
Note that multiplication by a scalar distributes over vector addition.
The velocity vector is multiplied by the scalar mass to give the momentum vector.
Dividing a vector by a nonzero scalar stretches or shrinks it along the same line.
In the exercise, take the product of the scalar 3 and the vector (2, -1).
quiet: In this course, students learn how to draw two vectors on a grid.
When you multiply a matrix by 2, every entry gets doubled.
A vector stretched by a factor of two keeps its direction but doubles in length.
Note that vector addition is commutative, so u + v equals v + u.
The velocity vector points in the direction in which the object is moving.
Dividing a vector by its own length gives a unit vector along the same line.
In the exercise, take the dot product of the vectors (1, 2) and (2, -1).

notes: Probe: 'product of a scalar and a matrix' 1.17 (peak ' and'), 'multiplied by a negative scalar' 0.85, __rmul__(self, scalar) 0.61; same operations without the word scalar are low ('scaled by constant factor k' 0.11, dot product 0.09, recipe by three 0.04), vector sum 0.25. Near misses keep vector/matrix multiplication but say 'number/factor'.
